chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan, who said:
I heard a man saying to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding al-nabeez? For Abu Maryam drinks it, and he claims that you have ordered with its drinking.'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Far be it from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that I should order with the drinking of an intoxicant. By Allah, it is something for which I fear the authorities, and nothing else.'
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every intoxicant is prohibited, therefore whatever a lot of it were to intoxicate, so a little of it is prohibited.'

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabeez (a specific type of fermented drink made from dates or raisins)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the prohibition of nabeez and the fear of authorities in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between absolute prohibition (haram) and precautionary avoidance (takhayyur) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam al-Sadiq (as) avoided 'al-nabeez' not due to intrinsic impurity but to prevent conflict with the Umayyad authorities who enforced its ban. It reinforces the foundational principle of 'kathiruhu wa qaliluhu haram' (much and little are both forbidden), linking the specific ruling on fermented date/water drinks to the broader Prophetic maxim that any substance causing intoxication in large quantities is prohibited even in small amounts.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan who said,
‘I heard a man saying to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘What are youasws saying regarding Al-Nabeez, for Abu Maryam is drinking it, and he claims that youasws have ordered with the drinking of it’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I seek Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic that I<sup>asws</sup> would be ordering with the drinking of an intoxicant. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! It is for something what I<sup>asws</sup> fear the authorities with regards to it, and not something else.
Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every intoxicant is Prohibited, therefore whatever a lot of it were to intoxicate, so a little of it is Prohibited’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hanan who has said the following:
“I once heard a man asking abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Nabidh and that abu Maryam drinks it and that he thinks he (the Imam) has commanded him to drink it.

He (the Imam) said, ‘I seek protection with Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, against commanding to drink intoxicating liquor. This by Allah is something about which I do not fear (Taqiyah, use caution before) the Sultan or people other than the Sultan.

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘All intoxicating liquor is unlawful. What is intoxicating in large quantity, it is unlawful in small quantity also.’”
